# Embassy 4.3.0 — Codex agents, discovered

4.3 removes the last piece of ceremony between a Codex task and a message: Codex agents no longer register themselves. Embassy discovers them.

**What changes for you** — every root agent the `codex agents` view lists, the twenty most recent by activity, appears in `embassy status` and the TUI within seconds of the broker starting, named after the thread (unnamed threads get a stable, typeable generated name). Working, waiting, ready and finished map to busy, waiting, idle and dormant. Sending to a dormant agent wakes it: Embassy resumes the thread and starts a turn, and the receipt comes back the same way it always has. Agents that fall out of the view's window stop being listed; a message to one of them is refused rather than guessed.

**Registration stays as the fallback** — a task in a harness without native integration still runs `embassy register-codex`, and a registered agent keeps its chosen name and its place regardless of the window. Discovered and registered agents are the same kind of endpoint; nothing marks one from the other.

**What Embassy will not do** — start, install or update the Codex daemon (`codex app-server daemon start` is yours, and the `codex agents` view offers it); answer approvals on an agent's behalf; steer an active turn with an ordinary message, which waits in the ledger until the turn ends, while an explicit `STEER:` still lands inside it. One honest limit: if another client starts a turn in the instant between Embassy's idle check and its write, the message enters that turn, and the App Server's reply cannot tell Embassy so; a receipt proves acceptance and lifetime, not that a fresh turn began. Sub-agents are never endpoints; only head agents are.

**The numbers** — private state schema 7 (a 4.2.0 file is read forward with every existing endpoint retained; no reset), local control protocol 6, federation protocol 3. Upgrade both machines and restart the brokers. Rollback to 4.2.0 needs the pre-upgrade backup, because 4.2.0 refuses schema 7.

**Tested with** (m5dev and a laptop over SSH, Codex CLI 0.153.4, 2026-09-06): parity with the agents view on both machines; a never-registered dormant thread woken on each, including the laptop's by discovered name across federation, both answering through the emitted reply command; three steers landing inside a running turn while an ordinary message waited; retirement without rediscovery; a Codex daemon restart with every discovered name unchanged; the registration fallback surviving discovery scans. Offline suite 394/394.
